ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a positive point charge $A$ with charge $Q=2{\times}10^{-7}\mathrm{C}$ is fixed at point $O$ in space. Another positive point charge $B$ with mass $m=2\times10^{-4}\mathrm{kg}$ and charge $q=1\times10^{-7}\mathrm{C}$ is released from rest at a point $0.5\mathrm{m}$ directly above $O$. During the motion of $B$, the point where its speed is maximum is at point $P$. Given the electrostatic constant $k{=}9{\times}10^{9}\mathrm{N{\cdot}m^{2}/C^{2}}$ and gravitational acceleration $g$ taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, find:

1. What is the magnitude of the acceleration when $B$ is released?
2. What is the distance $L$ between $P$ and $O$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a positive point charge $A$ with charge $Q=2{\times}10^{-7}\mathrm{C}$ is fixed at point $O$ in space. Another positive point charge $B$ with mass $m=2\times10^{-4}\mathrm{kg}$ and charge $q=1\times10^{-7}\mathrm{C}$ is released from rest at a point $0.5\mathrm{m}$ directly above $O$. During the motion of $B$, the point where its speed is maximum is at point $P$. Given the electrostatic constant $k=9{\times}10^{9}\mathrm{N\cdot m^{2}/C^{2}}$ and gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m/s^{2}}$, find: 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a vertical dashed line, with O and a fixed positive point charge A marked at the bottom; directly above it there is point P, and a positive point charge B is drawn beside it. On the right, a vertical double-headed arrow marks the distance from O to P as L, indicating that the direction of motion of B is along the vertical line directly above O, and P is above O. Reasoning: Take vertically upward as the positive direction, and let the distance from B to O be r. At release r0=0.5 m. Since A and B are both positive charges, the direction of the Coulomb force exerted by A on B is upward, with magnitude F_e=kQq/r0^2; the direction of gravity is downward, with magnitude mg. Calculate the electric field force at the instant of release: F_e=(9×10^9)(2×10^-7)(1×10^-7)/(0.5)^2=7.2×10^-4 N. Gravity: mg=(2×10^-4)(10)=2.0×10^-3 N. Therefore, taking upward as positive, the resultant force is F=F_e-mg=7.2×10^-4-2.0×10^-3=-1.28×10^-3 N. The acceleration a=F/m=(-1.28×10^-3)/(2×10^-4)=-6.4 m/s^2; the negative sign indicates downward, so the magnitude of the acceleration at release is 6.4 m/s^2. B initially accelerates downward; when B approaches O, the Coulomb repulsion increases. The position P where the speed is maximum corresponds to the acceleration along the direction of motion just becoming 0, that is, the resultant force is 0: kQq/L^2=mg. Thus L=sqrt(kQq/(mg))=sqrt((9×10^9×2×10^-7×1×10^-7)/(2×10^-4×10))=sqrt(0.09)=0.3 m. Final answer: the magnitude of the acceleration at the instant of release is 6.4 m/s^2; the distance L between P and O is 0.3 m.
